steps.title: Import React
steps.instruction: Import React from 'react' at the top of the file.
steps.hint: Add the import statement before any other code.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a library
import React from 'react';
steps.seedCode:
// Import React here

// Your component will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: React is imported and ready to use for JSX and components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React, which is essential for writing JSX and creating components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing React from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import syntax: you need to import React from 'react'.

steps.title: Create a Card component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Card that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a function called Card that returns JSX containing a <div> tag.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Card component function is defined that returns an empty div.
successCriteria: The code contains a Card component function that returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a Card component that returns an empty div.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named Card that returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named Card that returns a <div>.

steps.title: Add props parameter to Card
steps.instruction: Add a props parameter to the Card component function.
steps.hint: In the function definition, add parentheses with a parameter named props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component should accept props as a parameter.
successCriteria: The Card function has a props parameter in its parentheses.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The Card component now accepts props, which is the first step in making it reusable.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a parameter named props inside the parentheses of the Card function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component still doesn't have a props parameter. Add `props` inside the parentheses of the function.

steps.title: Access children from props
steps.instruction: Inside the Card component, destructure the children property from the props parameter.
steps.hint: You can use object destructuring to extract children directly from props in the function parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component will be ready to receive and use children content passed to it.
successCriteria: The Card component destructures children from its props parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully destructured the children prop, making it ready to use inside your Card component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're destructuring children directly from the props parameter in the Card function.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to destructure the children property from the props parameter in the Card component.

steps.title: Render children in Card
steps.instruction: Inside the Card component's return statement, render the children prop inside the div element.
steps.hint: Use JSX curly braces to output the children value inside the div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component will display any content passed as children inside a div.
successCriteria: The children prop is rendered inside the div using JSX curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered the children prop inside the Card component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're rendering the children prop inside the div using JSX curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The children prop needs to be rendered inside the div element using JSX curly braces.

steps.title: Create App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns JSX. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an App component that returns an empty div, ready to be used as the main component.
successCriteria: An App component is defined and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the App component returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named App that returns a div.

steps.title: Use Card with text children
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a Card component with the text 'Hello from children!' between its opening and closing tags.
steps.hint: Place the text directly between <Card> and </Card> tags, like you would with any HTML element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component renders a Card containing the text 'Hello from children!' as its children.
successCriteria: App returns a Card component with 'Hello from children!' placed between its opening and closing tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully passed text as children to the Card component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a Card, but make sure the text 'Hello from children!' is placed directly between the Card tags.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're adding a Card component with the exact text 'Hello from children!' as its children inside App's return statement.

steps.title: Use Card with element children
steps.instruction: Add another Card component inside the App's return statement, passing JSX elements (like an h1 and a p) as children.
steps.hint: Place a second Card component after the existing one, and nest JSX elements inside its opening and closing tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now contains two Card components: one with text children (from step 7) and one with JSX element children.
successCriteria: A second Card component is added in App's return statement, containing at least two nested JSX elements (e.g., h1 and p) as children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully passed JSX elements as children to the Card component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a second Card, but it might not contain the expected JSX elements as children. Ensure you nest elements like h1 and p inside the Card tags.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second Card with JSX element children is missing or incorrect. Add another Card component with nested JSX elements inside App's return.

steps.title: Add styling to Card
steps.instruction: Add CSS styles to the Card's div element to visually distinguish it. Use inline styles or a style object to add border, padding, and margin.
steps.hint: You can add a style attribute to the div. For example: style={{ border: '1px solid #ccc', padding: '16px', margin: '8px' }}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component's div will have visual styling (border, padding, margin) applied to make it stand out.
successCriteria: The Card's div element includes inline styles or a style object with at least border, padding, and margin properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added styling to the Card component, making it visually distinct.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some styles, but make sure to include border, padding, and margin for full visual distinction.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card's div doesn't have the required styling. Add border, padding, and margin using inline styles or a style object.

steps.title: Export App component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export from this file.
steps.hint: Use the 'export default' syntax to make the App component available for use in other files.
steps.analogousExample:
// Export a component as default
export default App;
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported as the default export, making it ready to be imported and rendered in other files.
successCriteria: The App component is exported as default using 'export default App;'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the App component as default. This makes it available for use in other parts of your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the correct export syntax: 'export default App;'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not exported correctly. Use 'export default App;' to export it as the default export.
